title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 16–25. New: CISA on Nov. 24 added Drupal Core, Idunno AntiCsrf, and Optimizely Web Experimentation to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, all due Nov. 27, and all require forensic triage. Palo Alto Networks said exploitation of a PAN-OS Linux-kernel flaw, CVE-2026-46300, has been seen against internet-exposed management interfaces. The Nov. 23 MONAI Label and MailAssure items remain due Nov. 26. No CISA KEV alert dated Nov. 25 was posted. The Nov. 16 Gootloader FLASH was retired. Puppet Enterprise CVE-2026-115731 remains due Dec. 1.

items.headline: CISA adds exploited Drupal, AntiCsrf, and Optimizely flaws, due Nov. 27
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 24 that it added three vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2026-132165 in Drupal Core, CVE-2026-131914 in Idunno AntiCsrf, and CVE-2026-132224 in Optimizely Web Experimentation. The catalog says an unauthenticated attacker can, under specific conditions, use Drupal's install.php to take over a site or execute code; that AntiCsrf lets an unauthenticated remote attacker execute code through object injection and may be end of life; and that Optimizely's signup flow can let an attacker impersonate a customer user and change Project JavaScript that then runs in browsers visiting that customer's sites. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 27, 2026, for all three, requires forensic triage for each, and lists ransomware use as unknown.

items.headline: CISA adds exploited MONAI Label and MailAssure flaws, due Nov. 26
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 23 that it added two vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2026-133968 in Project MONAI Label and CVE-2026-134624 in N-able MailAssure, also called SpamExperts. The catalog says MONAI Label lets an unauthenticated remote attacker write arbitrary files outside the datastore directory, potentially resulting in remote code execution. It says MailAssure's LDAP synchronization connection check lets an authenticated API user connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, see which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 26, 2026, for both, requires forensic triage for each, and lists ransomware use as unknown.

items.headline: CISA adds an exploited Puppet Enterprise flaw, due Dec. 1
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 17 that it added CVE-2026-115731, a Perforce Puppet Enterprise deserialization flaw, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. The catalog says a client with any certificate-authority-signed agent certificate can execute code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a crafted report, and that if the authority autosigns certificates, an unauthenticated attacker can obtain one. CISA lists a due date of Dec. 1, 2026, says ransomware use is unknown, and does not require forensic triage. The catalog entry links Perforce's advisory.

items.headline: Cairncross and Clayton say recent outages are not a coordinated cyberattack
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Nov. 20 that recent technology outages have not been linked to a cyberattack, and that work to patch AI-enabled software vulnerabilities has been connected to outages at the National Security Agency and several U.S. banks. Sean Cairncross told Semafor, in remarks Federal News Network quoted, that this is not a coordinated cyberattack and that he expects more disruptions from updating legacy systems. Axios reported Nov. 23 that administration officials say there is no evidence the outages were coordinated cyberattacks, and that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told lawmakers the outages appeared to stem from unrelated technical problems and system upgrades. Axios said Clayton, on ABC, declined to discuss reported cyberattacks on the FBI and the Department of Agriculture.

items.headline: Palo Alto says a PAN-OS kernel flaw is being used on exposed management interfaces
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks published security bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015, dated Nov. 25, for CVE-2026-46300, a Linux-kernel local privilege-escalation flaw it calls Fragnesia, in PAN-OS. The company said exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet. It said every observed case first used the PHP2Shell flaw, CVE-2026-109618, through that exposed interface, and that it is not aware of another method. Palo Alto Networks said customers whose management interface is reachable from the internet should upgrade immediately and restrict access to trusted internal addresses, and that others should upgrade at the next maintenance window.

items.headline: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo to shield Linux systems before a patch
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 23 that it and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that uses eBPF programs, called shields, to block vulnerable code paths on a running Linux system without a restart. OpenAI said operators can watch how a proposed shield would affect applications before enforcing it, that shields are cryptographically signed and checked by the Linux eBPF verifier, and that a Trusted Platform Module records when protections are loaded or removed. In a controlled test, OpenAI said a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service. OpenAI said Shirudo is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.

items.headline: CISA and Tom's Hardware: Java4Shell is an OpenJDK Base64 bug on newer server CPUs
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 17 that organizations should immediately patch Oracle Java CVE-2026-114938, which it calls Java4Shell, a memory-corruption bug in the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java virtual machine. CISA said specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and told defenders to find JDKs and Java runtimes, including copies bundled in applications, containers, and appliances, and to patch internet-facing systems first. The alert does not say the flaw is in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 19 that Calif Research, which found the bug, rates it 9.2 on CVSS 4.0, and that the flaw is in an OpenJDK Base64-decoding optimization that requires an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 and VBMI, which Tom's Hardware said means Intel Ice Lake and AMD Zen 4 server chips.

items.headline: ThreatLocker reproduces a Windows 11 lock-screen bypass that needs physical access
items.summary: ThreatLocker said Nov. 19 that its threat-intelligence team reproduced a Windows lock-screen bypass called FastUnlock, disclosed by a researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse. ThreatLocker said someone with physical access can open Microsoft Narrator during the Microsoft-account recovery flow and reach Windows settings without signing in, landing in the WSIAccount, which is not an administrator. ThreatLocker said the test required a Microsoft account available through account recovery and Narrator navigation, and that a BitLocker pre-boot PIN protects a machine that is powered off or hibernating because the PIN is required before Windows starts. ThreatLocker said it used an external drive in the proof of concept.
